correctness.rationale: Set p=e/(e−1), z=1+log(1−u/p)∈(0,1). Inverting the already defined FEx-G CDF gives (1−w)^w=z. Writing t=log(1−w)<0 transforms it to t e^t−t=−log z. H(t)=t(e^t−1) strictly decreases from +∞ at −∞ to 0 at 0− because H′=e^t(1+t)−1<0. Thus t is the unique negative r-Lambert W_{−1} branch and w=1−e^t; substituting G(x)=1−(1−x^a)^b gives Q=[1−exp(t/b)]^(1/a). This is mathematically correct for 0<u<1 and continuous strictly increasing baseline G.

originality.rationale: The original Eldemery et al FEx-G work supplies the full CDF and explicitly its already-inverted scalar relation w log(1−w)=log z; Mező–Baricz (2015/2017) define W_r as precisely the inverse of t e^t+r t and analyze real branches. The alleged exact FEx-G quantile is obtained immediately from that published relation by the one-step substitution t=log(1−w), setting the existing r parameter to −1 and composing with baseline G^{−1}. The branch restriction t<0 follows immediately from 0<w<1 and monotonicity of a known scalar function. The Kumaraswamy formula is algebraic substitution. The complete submitted claim is mathematically implied by these two prior statements, even without an identical named quantile formula. This is a covered corollary, not a distinct original theorem.
